note: class Circle : public Shape produces one extends edge, target spelled exactly as written at the base-list site ("Shape", unqualified) — the adapter does not type-resolve base names to their full FQN. Unlike C#, C++ has no separate interface keyword/edge kind: every base-list entry, interface-like or not, is correctly emitted as extends, so there is no interface_impl_gap analog here. The virtual destructor ~Shape() is a member symbol like any constructor/method; area() being `override` and `const` does not change its FQN (trailing qualifiers/virt-specifiers are stripped by definition, since the FQN is built from only the function name + parameter types).
